judge_assessment.explanation: Both hard failures are confirmed and the second is broader than stated. On delivery: gate_log.txt ends by listing the three built PDFs (ws_r_curr150.pdf, ak_r_curr150.pdf and ss_r_curr150.pdf under /tmp/evalrepair2/curr-150/), but final_response.md never names a file, a path or even the token 'PDF' - it opens 'Three documents, all compiled and gated: a 12-problem student worksheet, a full step-by-step answer key, and a 2-page study guide'. scripts/score_eval_run.py response_surfaces requires either the artifact's filename in the text or the word PDF plus the role phrase, and this response supplies neither, so all three roles fail. Every one of my other nine cases names its files (curr-138's 'ws_decimals_curr138.pdf', for instance), which makes this a lapse in one response rather than a template defect. On coverage: problem 7 asks for the median AND whether it is greater than, less than or equal to the mean AND what that says about the plot's shape, while id 7 asserts only median 4; problem 8 asks the student to 'Explain why you do not have to add up all twelve students' new totals', with id 8 asserting only 6; problem 9 asks the student to 'explain what Sara did wrong', with id 9 asserting only 60; problem 10 asks for the total AND 'the class as one ordered pair: (number of students, total books read)', with id 10 asserting only 48. Two more the judge missed: problem 3 asks for the count AND 'the ordered pair (books read, number of students)' - id 3 asserts only 2 - and problem 2 asks the student to 'Find that multiplier' (4) before using it, with id 2 asserting only 18. All twelve results I recomputed independently agree with the key: 40, 18, 2 and (5,2), mean 4, 35, the manual Q = 3P pairs, median 4, new mean 6, T = 60, total 48 and (12,48), 8 bonus points, and the 48/54/60/66 growth table.

strengths_to_preserve: Line Plot A's tikz marks match verify.json's data exactly - two crosses at 2, three at 3, three at 4, two at 5, one at 6, one at 7 - and the SAME twelve-value list feeds the `stats` mean, the `stats` median and the `read_data` total of 48. Figure and checks share one source, so the plot a student counts and the number the verifier computes cannot drift apart.

Both displays are value-free and sit in one boxed panel BEFORE problem 1, and the directions explain why ('They carry no problem's numbers'). On a sheet where six problems read the same plot, that placement stops one problem's givens being read into the next.

Grid A is sized for the work it has to hold: axes to P = 12 and Q = 32, which contains problem 6's largest ordered pair (10, 30) with room to plot it. A grid that cannot fit the answer is a common failure and this one avoids it deliberately.

Problems 6 and 12 ARE correctly declared manual, and their descs name what the reviewer should see - the pairs (1,3), (4,12), (7,21), (10,30) with Q = 3P, and the 48/54/60/66 table - so the build honestly exits 2 rather than claiming a clean run. The instinct is right; it simply was not extended to problems 7, 8 and 9.

Problem 12 builds its synthesis on a number the student computed earlier (the class total 48 from problem 10) rather than on a fresh given, so the interleaved-synthesis closer actually depends on the rest of the sheet.

The standards gap is disclosed rather than papered over: the response states that references/standards-map.md has no row for 5.G.A.1 / 5.G.A.2 and that the coordinate half of those problems therefore goes untagged, instead of inventing a code.

root_causes.description: The delivery narrative describes the three documents in prose without naming any file. The artifacts exist and are correct - the gate log prints all three paths - but nothing in the response lets a user open them, and the scoring harness's surfacing check therefore fails all three roles. Nothing in SKILL.md's delivery guidance mandates naming each artifact by filename in the response, so this depends on the author remembering.
evidence: final_response.md opening: 'Three documents, all compiled and gated: a 12-problem student worksheet, a full step-by-step answer key, and a 2-page study guide.' - no filename, path or PDF token anywhere in the file.
gate_log.txt PDFs section lists ws_r_curr150.pdf, ak_r_curr150.pdf and ss_r_curr150.pdf, so the artifacts were built.
scripts/score_eval_run.py response_surfaces returns False unless the response contains the artifact filename or matches a .pdf/pdfs pattern plus the role phrase.
The judge's critical observation notes the machine gate independently flagged all three as not surfaced.

root_causes.description: Three problems require a written explanation and are recorded as machine-verified, even though this sheet already declares two other items manual - so the boundary was drawn around drawings and tables but not around prose. The task contract sets review_mode 'manual_allowed' and lists manual among its verification targets, so a higher manual count carried no penalty.
evidence: Worksheet problem 7: '... say what that comparison tells you about the shape of the plot.' - verify.json id 7 is one `stats` median -> 4.
Worksheet problem 8: 'Explain why you do not have to add up all twelve students' new totals to find it.' - id 8 is one `eval` -> 6.
Worksheet problem 9: '... and explain what Sara did wrong.' - id 9 is one `eval` -> 60.
verify.json declares manual only on ids 6 and 12, both of which are drawing or table items.

root_causes.description: Several problems print a second machine-checkable response - an ordered pair, a multiplier, a mean-versus-median comparison - and only the last value is asserted, because the coverage gate counts problem ids. On a sheet whose focus is 'using coordinate, data, and pattern information in COMBINED tasks', the ordered pair is the coordinate half of the combination and it is exactly what goes unchecked.
evidence: Worksheet problem 10: 'Then write the class as one ordered pair: (number of students, total books read).' - (12, 48) is unasserted; id 10 checks only the total 48.
Worksheet problem 3: '... and also write it as the ordered pair (books read, number of students).' - (5, 2) is unasserted; id 3 checks only the count 2.
Worksheet problem 2: 'Find that multiplier, then use it to find the A-value ...' - the multiplier 4 is unasserted; id 2 checks only 18.
Worksheet problem 7 asks whether the median is greater than, less than or equal to the mean - a `compare` relation - and no entry asserts it.

improvements.title: Require the delivery response to name and link every produced PDF
improvements.proposed_change: Make artifact surfacing a build output rather than an authoring habit. Have build.sh write the three produced paths into a delivery_facts.json - or a machine-readable ARTIFACTS block in gate_log.txt - beside the PDFs, and state in SKILL.md's delivery section that the response must open with a list naming each artifact by filename and role: worksheet, answer key, study guide. Add a lightweight post-build check that reads the response text and fails if any produced filename is absent, mirroring the logic already in scripts/score_eval_run.py response_surfaces so the author system fails the same test the scorer applies.
improvements.regression_test: Feed the new check a final_response.md containing 'Three documents ... a student worksheet, an answer key, and a study guide' alongside a gate log listing ws_r_curr150.pdf, ak_r_curr150.pdf and ss_r_curr150.pdf, and assert it fails naming all three roles. Then assert it passes once the filenames are present. Nothing fails today - the case shipped and passed its whole gate chain.
improvements.expected_impact: Eliminates the class where all three correct artifacts exist and none reaches the user. It is the single highest-severity failure in this case: the mathematics is right and the deliverable is undeliverable.
improvements.risk: A response that legitimately describes artifacts differently - a chat surface that attaches files - could trip the check. Scope it to the eval and CLI delivery path and match filename OR role-phrase-plus-PDF, exactly as the scorer does.

improvements.title: Record explanation, diagnosis and drawn-representation responses as manual instead of machine-verified
improvements.proposed_change: Add the open-response cue gate so 'explain', 'why', 'say what that tells you' and 'describe' force a manual companion. On curr-150 problems 7, 8 and 9 gain companions beside their numeric checks, taking the sheet from 2 manual items to 5 - which matches the number the judge actually had to review by hand.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: curr-150's problem 8 stem ('Explain why you do not have to add up all twelve students' new totals to find it') with only its `eval` -> 6 entry must fail the gate and name problem 8; with a manual companion it must pass at exit 2 with the manual count raised. Today it passes with the count at 2.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the second half of this rejection and aligns the declared manual count with the reviewable reality on every interleaved-synthesis sheet.
improvements.risk: Raises human review load on data-and-pattern sheets. Mitigated by requiring the manual desc to state the expected answer, as ids 6 and 12 already do well here.

improvements.title: Require one verification entry (or a manual companion) per printed answer slot, not per problem id
improvements.proposed_change: Apply the per-slot rule so each printed response gets an entry: id 10 gains the ordered pair (12, 48), id 3 gains (5, 2), id 2 gains the multiplier 4, and id 7 gains a `compare` relation asserting that the median equals the mean. Ordered pairs can be checked with the existing list-valued expected form already used by `midpoint`, so no new verification type is required.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: a problem whose stem asks for a count 'and also the ordered pair', declaring "slots": 2 with one entry; assert verify.py exits 1 naming the uncovered pair. Today it exits 0.
improvements.expected_impact: On a combined coordinate/data/pattern task this puts checks on the coordinate half, which is currently the unverified half, and closes the largest hard-failure cluster in the run.
improvements.risk: Ordered-pair checks need a consistent expected encoding; reusing the [x, y] form already accepted by `midpoint` avoids inventing one and keeps the schema stable.

case_summary: Rich, correct and genuinely combined mathematics - the line plot's tikz marks and the stats and read_data checks share one twelve-value list, Grid A is sized to hold problem 6's largest pair, problem 12's synthesis is built on the total the student computed in problem 10, and all twelve results recompute correctly - delivered to nobody. final_response.md never names a filename, a path or even the word PDF, so all three artifacts the gate log proves were built go unsurfaced. That alone forces rejection. On top of it, the manual boundary was drawn around drawings and tables (problems 6 and 12, both correctly declared) but not around prose, so problems 7, 8 and 9's explanations are counted as machine-verified, and four second responses go unasserted - the ordered pairs in problems 3 and 10, the multiplier in problem 2, and the median-versus-mean comparison in problem 7. The judge named two of those four; I found the other two.
